en: Salutations to Śrī Gaṇeśa.
"By the mere knowledge of the syllable *oṃ*, I have been conquered by disease and indigestion;
I have fallen into the sleep of Time—save me, O Madhusūdana! (1)
No other refuge exists; you alone are my shelter.
I am submerged in the mire of sin; save me, O Madhusūdana! 2.
Deluded by the web of delusion regarding sons, wife, home, and the like, and being tormented by craving, I am [distressed]; save me, O Madhusūdana! (3)
O Lord, O Madhusūdana, protect me—who am devoid of devotion, wretched, afflicted by suffering and grief, without refuge, and without a protector. 4.
I am weary from coming and going throughout the long years of saṃsāra;
O Madhusūdana, protect me so that I may not go there again. 5.
Indeed, many various afflictions have been seen by me; there is great suffering in dwelling within the womb. Save me, O Madhusūdana! 6.
Therefore, O Lord, I have sought refuge in You, having You as my sole resort for protection;
O Madhusūdana, save me from being overwhelmed by the ocean of suffering. (7)
Whatever was promised by word and accomplished through action—that sin I have earned; I am in the fire, O Madhusūdana, save me! 8.
I have performed no good deed, yet I have committed evil;
I am submerged in the terrible ocean of saṃsāra—save me, O Madhusūdana! 9.
Throughout thousands of other bodies, I have been led astray from one to another, wandering through the states of animals and humans; O Madhusūdana, protect me! 10.
I speak as one who raves before you;
I am terrified by old age and death—save me, O Madhusūdana! (11)
Wherever I may go, among women or among men, may my devotion there remain unshakable; protect me, O Madhusūdana! (12)
The planets, such as the sun and the moon, return again and again after they have gone;
yet those who contemplate the twelve-syllable mantra do not return even to this day. (13)
"Vāsudeva has declared that there is nothing superior to the twelve-syllable mantra, which pervades the three worlds—the realm above, the netherworld, and the mortal world. (14)
The twelve-syllable great mantra, which bestows the fruits of all desires, was uttered by Śuka while dwelling in the womb. 15.
Whoever, fasting, recites the twelve-syllable mantra on the day of Hari, that Vaiṣṇava shall go to the abode of Viṣṇu, where Hari, the Lord of Yoga, resides. (16)
Thus ends the Madhusūdana-stotra composed by the venerable Śukadeva.
